payload.acceptance_criteria:
When basicly build runs twice in a row with no source change, git status shall stay clean.
A gate or a test shall prove the two-build clean state.
Before generated_at is removed or made content-derived, a search for every reader of the manifest generated_at shall run with a known-match control, and its counts shall be on this record.
payload.description:
## Context
When basicly build runs twice with no source change, I want git status to stay clean, so I can land a lane without timestamp-only commits and two lanes never conflict on one line.
basicly build writes a wall-clock generated_at into the tracked file .basicly/generated-manifest.json (src/basicly/cli.py:323, _build_manifest). On 2026-11-13 the .43.37 landing needed three timestamp-only commits in harness/m5-v4d-3 (1c84ec49, 49be6170, f383f57c). Decided by the orchestrator 2026-11-13 (owner go on parallel work). Builder: the Codex session in its own lane after a MAIN-FREE entry; do not claim it here.
payload.title: Keep basicly build from dirtying the manifest when no source changed

payload.acceptance_criteria:
While a landing holds the lock, a second basicly worktree merge shall wait or exit with a refusal that names the holder and the lock age.
The lock file shall hold an owner id and an age limit, and a lock older than the limit shall be reported by name, not taken silently.
payload.description:
## Context
When two sessions land lanes into one main, I want the second landing to wait or be refused by name, so I can stop relying on a lock line in a text file that agents must remember.
Today the lock is the MAIN-BUSY line in the orchestrator channel file. Decided by the orchestrator 2026-11-13 (owner go). Build after the vault cutover (.43.34).
payload.title: Give basicly worktree merge a real landing lock

payload.acceptance_criteria:
When the landing refuses a lane with REBASE-MERGE-COMMIT, it shall print a command or offer a mode that lands the lane's own commits onto main without rewriting the lane branch.
When the landing names no worktree session for a branch, it shall print the command that registers or recreates that session.
payload.description:
## Context
When basicly worktree merge refuses a lane, I want the refusal to print the exact command that fixes it, or a mode that replays the lane's own commits onto main, so I can land without a hand rewrite.
Evidence 2026-11-13 on .43.37: REBASE-MERGE-COMMIT on harness/m5-v4d (merge commit 8f03025a) and "no worktree session named 'm5-v4d-2'" for a branch made with git worktree add. Decided by the orchestrator 2026-11-13 (owner go). Build after the vault cutover (.43.34).
payload.title: Print the fixing command when the landing tool refuses a lane

payload.acceptance_criteria:
When a commit marked work in progress is made on a never-pushed lane branch, the commit hook shall let it pass.
When a marked commit is made on main, the commit hook shall refuse it.
When a landing or a push range holds a marked commit, the landing gate and the pre-push hook shall refuse it by name.
payload.description:
## Context
When a process ends during lane work, I want the lane's unfinished work kept in a commit, so I can lose nothing; handily lost uncommitted work of two lanes when a process ended on 2026-11-12.
Decided by the orchestrator 2026-11-13 (owner go). Build after the vault cutover (.43.34).
## Risk
This could become a way around the gates: an agent marks real work as work in progress to skip checks, then lands it or pushes the branch. Prevention: the marker is accepted only on a branch that was never pushed and is not main; the landing gate and the pre-push hook refuse any range that holds a marked commit; the full verify at landing stays strict; a marked commit cannot close a record.
payload.title: Let a marked work-in-progress commit pass on a never-pushed lane branch
